name: Northern Germany (North German Plain · Hamburg · Berlin)

language.script_notes: Low German (Plattdeutsch) dialect and some Frisian appear on informal/cultural signage near the North Sea coast.

road_furniture.curb_style: Thatched roofs and low stone/rock walls appear in North Frisian and Baltic coastal resort towns.

architecture.roof_style: Steep gabled roofs on brick Gothic townhouses and churches; thatched roofs on the North Frisian Islands and Baltic coast.
architecture.roof_material: Red, sometimes yellow, green or black-glazed brick and tile; thatch on traditional coastal houses.
architecture.wall_construction: Red brick Gothic (Backsteingotik) construction is the region's defining architectural signature — tall brick churches, gabled merchant townhouses (especially in Hanseatic League cities like Lübeck, Hamburg, Rostock, Stralsund).
architecture.wall_color_palette: Deep red/brown brick dominates; whitewashed thatched cottages on the coast and islands.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Brick Gothic churches and gabled Hanseatic merchant houses; Hamburg's warehouse district (Speicherstadt); thatched-roof coastal cottages; Berlin's mix of Prussian formal architecture and modern rebuilding.

nature.vegetation: Flat farmland, heath and marsh across the North German Plain; coastal dunes and salt marsh along the North Sea/Baltic coasts; scattered woodland.
nature.terrain: Very flat and low-lying — the North German Plain, geest and heath inland, marshland along the coast; the North Sea and Baltic Sea coastlines with offshore islands (North Frisian Islands, Rügen).
nature.climate_signature: Flat, open, often windy and overcast — a noticeably lower, flatter horizon than the south's Alpine backdrop.

vehicles.plate_color: Single-letter city codes for the largest cities (B = Berlin, HH = Hamburg).

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4, very dense in Berlin/Hamburg.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring; notably more opted-out/blurred building façades in some residential areas, a broader German quirk.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense urban coverage; good rural coverage across the flat plain.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat low-lying terrain, similar orderly infrastructure, coastal marsh and dune landscape
confusion_set.tiebreaker: German plates/vocabulary differ from Dutch yellow-plate signage; North German brick Gothic architecture (Lübeck/Hamburg style) is heavier and taller than typical Dutch townscapes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, plate and bollard style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The north is flat with brick Gothic architecture and a low coastal horizon; the south is mountainous with half-timbered/Alpine chalet architecture and onion-domed churches.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar brick Gothic Hanseatic architecture in shared former Hanseatic League towns along the Baltic
confusion_set.tiebreaker: German plates and vocabulary vs. Polish plates and Polish-language signage; the built brick style is closely related but signage settles it immediately.
